components.name: ECDSA-secp256k1 (BIP39/BIP32 HD wallet, Ethereum tx signing)

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js@1.1.3 is a real lockfile dependency (transitive via elliptic, pulled in by the web3 Ethereum stack). It ships SHA-1/SHA-2 implementations to the build; no direct first-party call site, but it is part of the dependency inventory. Cross-reference: LIB-e966a74e (hash.js) is the same package seen as a library record.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Lockfile declaration of the secp256k1 curve packages (secp256k1, libp2p-crypto-secp256k1) shipped by this Ethereum e-voting app's dependency tree (web3 + ipfs-api). This is the live transaction-signature curve of the application — every vote is an ECDSA-secp256k1-signed Ethereum transaction — reached through web3 rather than a direct require. Changeable only by migrating the chain stack, not by editing the lockfile entry.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: First-party password hashing for company and voter accounts (bcrypt@^3.0.6, cost/saltRounds 10). Live chains: pre-save hooks hash on create (models/company.js:18, models/voter.js:22), company login verifies with compareSync (controllers/company.js:38), controllers/voter.js:140 re-hashes on update. Posture notes a fixer should see: voter registration stores the voter's EMAIL as the password (controllers/voter.js:23) and emails it in cleartext; voter authenticate (controllers/voter.js:93) queries

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Lockfile declaration of the evp_bytestokey package — OpenSSL's EVP_BytesToKey single-round MD5 KDF — shipped transitively via the browserify-crypto shim chain that web3/ipfs-api pull in. Part of the shipped build; weak-KDF practice flag is correct, but no first-party call site invokes it directly.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency-inventory entry: create-ecdh@4.0.0 (node's createECDH shim) ships with the web3/browserify stack this e-voting dapp builds on; classical ECDH is retroactively breakable (harvest-now-decrypt-later class), but here it sits in transitive library code, replaceable only by upgrading the Ethereum toolchain, not by editing app code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Lockfile-level entry for elliptic@6.4.1, the secp256k1 ECDSA provider of the Ethereum stack. The app-level signing uses (server deploy via truffle-hdwallet-provider at Ethereum/deploy.js:19, client vote/election-creation via MetaMask at pages/election/vote.js:123 and pages/election/create_election.js:24) are reported as separate findings since the deterministic pass only saw the lockfile. Classical ECDSA is Shor-vulnerable.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: three scrypt implementations (scrypt@6.0.2, scrypt-js@2.0.4, scrypt.js@0.2.0) ship in the build as transitive deps of the web3/ganache Ethereum toolchain (web3 keystore/V3 key-file derivation). Quantum-safe password KDF; iteration parameters live inside the libraries, not in app code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak-256 (Ethereum's pre-FIPS-202-padding SHA-3 variant) is the hash of the whole system: the web3 stack deps provide it in JS, and the compiled contracts' EVM bytecode uses the SHA3 opcode (storage-slot hashing, solc ^0.4.25). Quantum-safe (Grover gives only square-root speedup).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: pbkdf2@3.0.17 is a transitive dep (crypto-browserify stack); the same primitive is also what derives the HDWalletProvider seed (BIP39 PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512, 2048 iterations) from the hardcoded mnemonic at Ethereum/deploy.js:6-8. Quantum-safe KDF; parameters live in libraries, not app code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge@0.7.6 ships AES among its primitives and is built by this project (transitive dep of the Ethereum/web3 toolchain). No first-party AES call site in the application. Note for remediation: 0.7.6 is a 2019-era release with publicly known vulnerabilities since (e.g. CVE-2020-7720); upgrade path exists independent of PQ concerns.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl ships Ed25519, X25519 and XSalsa20-Poly1305 with the web3 account tooling of this e-voting dapp. Both sites are lockfile-level; no first-party call site in the app. The Ed25519/X25519/XSalsa20 capability objects sit in scout 1's shard — same underlying package.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Same node-forge@0.7.6 package as the AES entry (ALG-0eb2c0da) — one logical dependency, two capability names. Its X.509 machinery ships in the build via the web3/truffle toolchain; no first-party certificate handling in the app.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js@2.0.4 is one of the three scrypt packages in the scrypt object (ALG-c1f8b585); it ships with web3 for keystore key derivation.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic@6.4.1 provides the secp256k1 ECDSA the web3 stack signs with; linked to the ECDSA capability entry ALG-710f61f0 so a reader references one entry.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js@1.1.3 (ethereumjs hash utility: keccak/sha256/ripemd160) ships as a transitive dep of the web3 stack; no first-party call site in the app. Distinct package from elliptic/pbkdf2 — kept as its own entry.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: pbkdf2@3.0.17 is the same package as the PBKDF2 algorithm entry ALG-4de3b020; linked so a reader references one entry. Ships with the crypto-browserify/web3 stack.
